Hi Samir — thanks for the note and the form. Quick answers inline and below; Marissa (reliability lead) is looped in for details and the dashboard walkthrough. We can also schedule a 30-min demo this week.

High-level:
- Measurement: Availability is measured as successful request ratio over a 30-day rolling window; latency SLOs are measured at p50/p95/p99 depending on the SKU (default public SKU uses p95). Error budget is calculated daily and reported in the dashboard.
- Monitoring stack: We emit Prometheus-style metrics and have a Grafana tenant per account for customer viewing (link and invite provided by Marissa). Metric retention for customer-visible metrics is 90 days by default; detailed telemetry (sampling traces, raw logs) can be retained longer under contract.
- Customer access: We provide read-only Grafana dashboards and per-route tokenized query access for customers. Raw telemetry for audits is available as a time-limited export (CSV/Parquet) upon request; retention and exports are scoped in the contract.
- Alerting & notifications: We operate a PagerDuty rotation for sev1/sev2 and will forward customer-facing incident notifications by email+workspace webhook. Customers can opt-in to real-time incident webhooks.
- Exception process: We have a documented SLA exception path (internal review + customer request form). Short-term SLO relaxations can be approved for scheduled migration windows with agreed mitigations or for one-off infra events.

I'm attaching our SLO playbook for procurement review. Proposed next steps: 1) Marissa to send Grafana invite and metric matrix; 2) schedule a 30-min walkthrough; 3) if HealthCorp needs an exception draft, we'll start the internal review once we receive the proposed window.

Best,
Logan Wright
Enterprise Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Samir — hi, Marissa on reliability. Adding the technical detail you asked for below and attaching the metrics matrix.

Definitions & measurement windows (concrete):
- Availability: successful 2xx/3xx responses divided by total requests for the customer tenant over a 30-day rolling window; measured in 1-minute buckets aggregated to daily and 30-day windows.
- Latency: aggregated per-route; we compute p50/p90/p95/p99 on the server-side using t-digest summaries per 5-minute aggregation windows, then roll to 1h/24h/30d windows for reporting. Default SLA uses p95 over 30 days unless otherwise contracted.
- Error budget: daily burn rate is computed; we publish the remaining budget on the customer dashboard and expose an alert when projected burn exceeds configurable thresholds (default: 50% of budget used within 7 days).

Monitoring & telemetry:
- Metrics exposed: redwood.request.count, redwood.request.errors, redwood.request.latency_ms (labels: model, route, region, tenancy). Customers see these in their Grafana tenant with read-only permissions.
- Retention: customer-facing aggregates: 90 days. Raw per-request telemetry: retained for 14 days by default; can be extended to 180/365 days under contract with a retention addendum.
- Sampling: we sample traces at adaptive rates; errors are always captured.

Alerts & customer notification:
- Incident classification: sev1 (availability impact), sev2 (degraded latency), sev3 (partial feature impact). Sev1/Sev2 triggers PagerDuty immediately and sends an incident summary to configured customer webhooks and email.
- SLO alerts: we provide both trend alerts (projected burn) and threshold alerts (instant drops below threshold). Customers can subscribe to both.

Exception path & temporary relaxations:
- Formal request: customer submits the SLO Exception Form (attached). Internal review (SRE + Legal + Account) within 48 business hours.
- Options: approved temporary slack (e.g., 1.5x p95 objective) for short windows (<=72h) with mitigation plans; longer relaxations require escalation and may involve pro-rated credits.
- Audit trail: all exception approvals are recorded with rationale, dates, and duration.

Attachments: slo-metrics-matrix.xlsx (metric names, Prometheus labels, retention), example alert rules, and exception form.

Grafana invite: https://redwood.app/grafana/invite/abcd-1234 (will expire after 7 days).

I can run a 30-min walkthrough Wed or Thu afternoon PT.

—Marissa

Samir — quick confirmation for inclusion in the procurement packet. Short answers below and next steps.

1) Scheduled migration exceptions: We support scheduled SLO relaxations for planned maintenance. Process: submit SLO Exception Form (attached) with window, rollback plan, and mitigation. Standard approval timeline is 48 business hours overhead; for scheduled events we typically pre-approve requests submitted at least 7 days in advance. Typical options we offer: 72-hour temporary slack at 1.5x p95 with no credit, or 72-hour slack at 2x p95 with a negotiated pro-rated credit. Exact terms are contract-specific and will be included as an addendum.

2) Audit exports & redaction: We can provide time-limited exports in Parquet or CSV, with optional redaction rules (replace PII fields with hashed tokens). Exports are delivered via secure S3 link with short-lived credentials and we log access for auditability. Retention for this export period can be set to 30 days post-migration per your request — we'll include that in the service annex.

3) Dashboard walkthrough: Confirming Marissa will host the 30-min session; attendees from Redwood: Marissa (reliability) and Vivek (account SRE). HealthCorp attendees: Aisha Rahman and Irene Choi — welcome. Proposed times: Thu 5/7 2:00–2:30pm PT or Fri 5/8 10:00–10:30am PT. Please confirm a slot and we'll send calendar invites.

Next steps: 1) HealthCorp to return SLO Exception Form if they want a pre-approved migration window; 2) we'll provision Grafana read-only access and prepare the export checklist for the procurement packet.
